text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/12/10 - 01 - Essay
Buildings and streets form a city neighborhood.
Pexels · 21576133
Getting to know a city
There is more than one way to explore a neighbourhood. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to
others are two useful starting points.
One reason is that walking slowly helps us notice details we usually miss. For instance, we stop to look at a doorway
instead of hurrying to the next landmark. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also
leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that respecting local routines makes a visit more considerate. For example, we keep an entrance
clear while taking a photograph of the street. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than
one person and that different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail.
We can make a sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Make a sentence of your own, then answer: What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two
reasons are that walking slowly helps us notice details we usually miss and that respecting local routines makes a visit more
considerate. One example is that we stop to look at a doorway instead of hurrying to the next landmark.)
